info.name: Agilis Advertising API
info.description:
Generated from https://www.agilis.dating/openapi.json by tools/build_postman.py (OpenAPI 1.0.0).

Use the Test environment and a Test key (pk_test_...). [write] requests change data; [spends] requests can charge money in Live mode. Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

request.description:
Returns all active categories available to the organisation that owns the API key. It is typically called before creating an offer, because offer creation requires a valid category ID returned by this endpoint.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Returns the interests available for offer targeting. Call it before creating an offer if you intend to use the optional `interests` array, which restricts the offer to users who have selected at least one of the interests supplied.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Calculates what an offer will cost before it is created: its size in Ad Units (duration in hours × the number of Agilis users it would reach) and what those units cost in money. Only active, non-banned accounts are counted. Pass the same `gender` and `interests` values you intend to create the offer with, otherwise the estimate will be higher than the amount actually charged.

`price_estimate` is a number of **Ad Units**, not money. `estimated_cost` is the **money** the offer will cost, and is the figure to compare with your balance.

There is no `currency` parameter: the estimate is always in your organisation's billing currency, named in the response's `currency` field.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

header.description: A unique value you generate per offer (for example a UUID v4). Replaying the same key safely retries the request without creating a duplicate offer or a second Stripe payment; the original response, including any `payment_url`, is returned verbatim. Missing: HTTP 400 / `E1`.

request.description:
Creates a new offer for the authenticated advertiser. The request is sent as `multipart/form-data` with the offer image supplied as a binary file stream. The image is checked by automated content moderation before the offer is created: if it fails, nothing is created and nothing is charged.

**Paying by Stripe link** (`payment_method=E`): the offer is created in **Awaiting Payment** and the response carries a `payment_url`. Stripe's `checkout.session.completed` webhook activates it: **Active** if its start has passed, **Scheduled** if not. An organisation registered in the UK pays VAT at 20% on top, as a separate line on the Stripe page. Stripe will not take a card payment below its minimum for the currency (for example £0.30, US$0.50 or €0.50): such an offer is refused with `E1`.

**Paying from balance** (`payment_method=B`): the offer's price is deducted at once, from the balance of the offer's own mode (TEST and LIVE balances are separate). Compare your balance with `estimated_cost` from the price estimate, never `price_estimate`.

There is no `currency` parameter: every offer is priced and charged in your organisation's billing currency, named in the response.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

request.description:
Returns a **paginated** list of offers created by the authenticated advertiser for the requested environment, newest first. Offers whose image was rejected by content moderation are never created, so they are not returned, and deleted offers are excluded. Page through results with `limit` and `cursor`.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Pauses a running offer. The offer must belong to the account that owns the API key and be in the key's mode (TEST or LIVE). Any other offer returns HTTP 401 with `E1`. Time spent paused is Unused Time: it is credited to your balance if you later delete the offer.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Resumes a paused offer. The offer must belong to the account that owns the API key and be in the key's mode. Any other offer returns HTTP 401 with `E1`.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Returns view and click metrics for a specific offer over the requested time interval. The offer must belong to the account that owns the API key and be in the key's mode.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Deletes an offer belonging to the authenticated account, in your API key's mode (an offer of the other mode is not found).

**Awaiting Payment:** the offer's Stripe payment page is closed first, so it can no longer be paid. If Stripe reports that the payment has just been completed, or the page cannot be closed, nothing is deleted (`E6`, `E7` below).

**Paid offers** (Active, Scheduled or Paused): the offer's Unused Time is credited to your balance in the offer's own mode. Unused Time is the part of the scheduled period in which the offer did not run: the time from the deletion to the scheduled end, plus any time it spent paused. An offer deleted before it starts is credited in full. The credit is net of VAT and goes to your balance, never back to a card.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Returns the Agilis event categories, **for display**: for example to label an event in your own system with the category the API chose for it. It is not an input. The category of an event is determined from its title, description and venue name (see [Preview Event](https://www.agilis.dating/api-doc#previewEventSectionid)). Names are returned in the language of your `Accept-Language` header, falling back to English.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

The currency codes a ticket price may be quoted in: every currency with an exchange rate on file, which is what lets the app sort events by price across currencies. Use one of these for `currency` on publish and edit. This is the currency members see on the price pill; it has no effect on what you are charged.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

What publishing costs your organisation, your balance, whether LIVE publishing is open, the accepted currencies and the image limits. Useful before a publish, or to show the fee in your own system. `listing_fee` is £10 converted at the day's European Central Bank reference rate into your organisation's billing currency (`currency`); `exchange_rate_per_gbp` is the rate used and `exchange_rate_date` its date (`1` and `null` for GBP). All three are `null` when your billing currency cannot be billed right now (see `E6` on Publish Event). `environment` is your API key's mode (`TEST` or `LIVE`), and `balance` and `organisation_balance` are the balances for that mode: **TEST and LIVE balances are separate**, so a TEST key never shows the LIVE balance.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Shows you what `POST /events` would do, **without publishing or charging**: the category your wording will get, the fee and your balance, and — if you include an image — the processed picture with its 16:9 crop applied, plus a `preview_token` that `POST /events` accepts instead of the file, so the published image is byte-for-byte the one you saw. Same fields as `POST /events`; `image` and `payment_method` are optional and no `Idempotency-Key` is needed. A rejected image returns `E2` here, before any payment. **Rate-limited** per organisation (60 previews per hour): each preview costs an image check and a classification.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

JPG or PNG, detected from the file's content (not its name), up to **10 MB**, at least **1280 × 720** pixels. Members see events at 16:9: the image is scaled to fill a 16:9 frame with its centre kept and the overflow trimmed (a *centred cover crop*), never stretched or letterboxed. Pass `crop[x]`, `crop[y]`, `crop[w]` to choose the area yourself. If the area would be below 1280 × 720 the image is rejected rather than enlarged. request.description:
Publishes one dated event. Sent as `multipart/form-data`. Publishing costs one flat price, deducted from your balance: **£10, converted into your organisation's billing currency at the day's European Central Bank reference rate**. The charge and the event are created together: if your balance is too low, nothing is created and nothing is charged. Listings are **non-refundable** once published, including if you later cancel. A recurring class is one event per date. **There is no `category_id`:** the category is determined from your title, description and venue name and returned in the response — preview it first if you want to see it before paying.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

request.description:
Returns events, newest first, with cursor pagination in the same envelope as `GET /offers`. **Who sees what:** an organisation admin's key sees every event in the organisation, whoever created it; a developer's key sees the whole organisation's events read-only; an advertiser's key sees its own. `attendees` is always a **band** (`<10`, `10-25`, `26-50`, `50+`), never an exact number: member privacy comes first, and an exact count on a small event would let attendance be inferred.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

One event: the same fields as the list, plus what it cost (`listing_price`, `billing_currency`, `invoice_id`), whether you may change it (`can_manage`, `can_delete`), whether members have interacted with it, the stored image's size and crop (`image_master`), and its `history`: every action taken on it, by whom and when.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Changes a published event, **free of charge**. Send only the fields to change. Editable: title, description, booking page, ticket price, venue and image. **Not dates** — use Reschedule. A wording change re-determines the category, which the response returns; preview first if you want to see it. A new image goes through the same checks as on publish and is stored at new URLs (invitations already sent keep the picture they were sent with). Members see the change within a few minutes. When uploading a file, send the request as `POST` with the header `X-HTTP-Method-Override: PATCH`, because file uploads need a POST body. **You remain responsible for telling everyone who booked through your own booking system** about any change; Agilis may notify its members but does not guarantee it.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

request.description:
Removes an event that no member has interacted with yet, for example one published by mistake. Once any member has marked themselves as going, invited someone, or opened your booking page, the event can no longer be deleted: cancel it instead, so those members are told. Deleting does not return the listing fee.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Moves a published event to a new date, at no charge. Within a few minutes the app shows the new date, and anyone who had accepted an invitation to the event is asked to confirm again, because nobody has agreed to the new date yet. **You are responsible for informing everyone who booked through your own booking system** of the change and the reason for it; Agilis may notify its members but does not guarantee it, and is not responsible for communication about your event. Use this rather than cancelling and publishing again.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Cancels a published event. **Irreversible, and the listing fee is not refunded.** Within a few minutes the app marks it cancelled and every open or accepted invitation to it is cancelled. **You are responsible for informing everyone who booked through your own booking system**; Agilis may notify its members but does not guarantee it. Please cancel rather than leaving a listing up for an event that is not running, so nobody turns up to a closed door. No request body.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc

Returns engagement for one event over the requested interval. Figures are refreshed every few minutes; `as_of` says when, and is `null` until the first member interaction.

Reference: https://ads.agilis.dating/api-doc
